trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Financial Advise AIFA: Everyday Banking (FAIS)
Company: Absa Group
About the company: With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: To follow the six steps of financial planning in executing the role of a FAIS licensed financial adviser. A professional introduction must be made to introduce the adviser and the services offered by the adviser. Upon client approval the adviser may conduct a Financial Needs Analysis (FNA) in the disciplines of Investment, Life Insurance and Estate planning. Based on the concluded FNA to make recommendations
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Participate in reciprocal leads activities and sales/pipeline meetings to identify opportunities for new or repeat business, and fully utilising Absa’s bancassurance structure.
  - Assess client’s needs through use of recommended needs analysis tools, ensuring that the client is aware of the full value proposition offered by AIFA.
  - Prepare recommendation and quote for appropriate risk and investment solutions based on the client’s individual needs and profile.
  - Present recommendation to clients, ensuring that all FAIS regulations are followed regarding advice given.
  - Follow all the steps in the designated client engagement process as specified by Absa Advisers.
  - Provide regular feedback to the Regional Manager on actions taken to progress the lead to business.
  - Network, on an ongoing basis, with all stakeholders in Everyday Banking (PGM’s and Regional Managers) and elsewhere by attending their meetings and social gatherings to position the Absa Advisers' value proposition to the Bank and to the clients
  - Do activity planning by identifying the clients to be approached/contacted during a particular period in conjunction with Everyday Advice Executive.
  - Using the leads information provided by the source and or Regional Manager listings, as well as leads sourced through own prospecting activities and determine the client's financial needs.
  - Make exclusive use of Absa’s Financial Needs Analysis tool (Avalon from Aug 2024 onwards) to conduct a comprehensive Financial Needs Analysis for the client.
  - Obtain the client's consent to access his/her existing policy information by getting him/her to sign the relevant documents to get a comprehensive view of the client's financial needs.
  - Discuss various possible solutions and options available with the client and thereafter recommend the most appropriate products and or solution(s) to address financial needs.
  - Generate and discuss a formal recommendation including product quote(s) for the client.
  - On acceptance of part or all the advice recommendations, complete the necessary product application forms and ensure that the client signs the forms to indicate his/her consent to engage in a transaction(s).
  - Gather, generate, and complete all the necessary compliance documentation (e.g., Client Advice Record, copy of ID, Financial Needs Analysis, FICA).
  - Submit the proposal forms to the relevant product providers for processing.
  - Ensure that the issued policy aligns to the recommended product.
  - Review the client's portfolio at a minimum of once a year and contact the client based on the adviser and client agreed contact strategy to maintain a healthy client relationship.
  - Provide a report back to the Regional Manager and Everyday Banking stakeholders on the strike rate (i.e., the number of leads provided that were converted to business) where applicable.
  - Seek business opportunities from external sources as necessary to grow the book of business and reciprocate leads to Regional Managers and PGM’s.
  - Capture the correct Policy Relevant Information (PRI) number on the Commission system.
  - On a monthly basis, check the accuracy of the commission statements received from the Broker Commissions department.
  - Verify that all the PRI numbers reconcile to the commission paid and reflected on the statements Keep the client database up to date by ensuring that new clients are added to the database.
  - Follow up on unpaid premiums and lapses by contacting the clients to establish the reasons for the problems Manage the suspense account timeously by clearing it on the system at month end.
  - Ensure that staff members (Adviser Assistants) have a clear understanding of their roles and responsibilities within the adviser practice.
  - Arrange for staff members to receive the relevant training (Absa programs for the Interns) e.g., systems training, product training and operational training.
  - Provide coaching and mentoring to assistant(s) with regards to facilitate knowledge and skills development.
  - Participate performance development (PD) discussions as required by the Absa performance management standards.
  - Take the necessary corrective actions in cases of underperformance in consultation with the Regional Manager.
  - Implement controls with regards to compliant record keeping in accordance with minimum Absa business standards (i.e. FAIS, FICA, FSB and)
  - Liaise with Provincial Operations Office) with regards to maintenance of systems and equipment and provision of other services
  - Complete all the required compliance exams in the specified timeframes (e.g. Anti-Money Laundering, Sanctions, BCM, Basic Financial Crime Concepts).
  - Remain fit and proper as required for FAIS flagged roles.
  - Provide monthly feedback to the branch, and Business Bank, regarding non-interest income (seat costs) and cross-selling opportunities
  - Segment the client base according to profile, income potential and commission income.
  - Engage with business development strategies with the support of the Regional Manager and our practice management subject matter experts to maximise the sustainability of the adviser practice.
  - Attend all the required training to attain accreditation to market Absa approved products.
  - Attend all the requisite internal training (i.e FAIS-related programs/courses).
  - Attain the required FAIS credits in order to attain Fit and Proper status
  - Ensure that Fit and Proper status is maintained (honesty, integrity, financial solvency)
Must-have requirements:
  - Minimum 2-3 years Financial Planning / Advice in Long-term Insurance and investment
  - NQF 5 FSB approved qualification (120 FAIS Credits)
  - RE 5 Certification
  - Fit and proper for typical license categories
  - Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Business, Commerce and Management Studies (Required)
Location: Vredendal
Team notes: Everyday Banking, reporting to the Regional Manager
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

Financial Adviser (FAIS) – Everyday Banking

Absa Group

Vredendal

About us
With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.

About the role
You will work as a FAIS licensed financial adviser, following the six steps of financial planning. You introduce yourself and your services to clients, and with their approval conduct a Financial Needs Analysis across investment, life insurance and estate planning. Based on that analysis, you make recommendations. The role sits in Everyday Banking in Vredendal and reports to the Regional Manager.

Your team
Everyday Banking, reporting to the Regional Manager

What you'll do
• Assess client needs using Absa's Financial Needs Analysis tool (Avalon from August 2024 onwards), and obtain client consent to access existing policy information.
• Prepare and present formal recommendations and product quotes for risk and investment solutions, following all FAIS regulations on advice given.
• Complete product application forms on acceptance of advice, and submit proposal forms to product providers for processing.
• Gather and complete compliance documentation, including Client Advice Record, copy of ID, Financial Needs Analysis and FICA, and keep records in line with Absa business standards.
• Check that each issued policy aligns to the recommended product.
• Review each client's portfolio at least once a year and contact clients per the agreed contact strategy.
• Participate in reciprocal leads activities and pipeline meetings, and use leads from the Regional Manager, Absa's bancassurance structure and your own prospecting.
• Network with Everyday Banking stakeholders (PGMs and Regional Managers) by attending their meetings and gatherings to position the Absa Advisers value proposition.
• Report to the Regional Manager and Everyday Banking stakeholders on strike rate, and give the branch and Business Bank monthly feedback on non-interest income (seat costs) and cross-selling opportunities.
• Segment the client base by profile, income potential and commission income, and keep the client database up to date.
• Check commission statements from Broker Commissions monthly, capture correct PRI numbers, reconcile PRI numbers to commission paid, and clear the suspense account at month end.
• Follow up with clients on unpaid premiums and lapses to establish the reasons.
• Coach and mentor Adviser Assistants, clarify their roles, arrange systems, product and operational training, and hold performance development discussions.
• Liaise with the Provincial Operations Office on maintenance of systems and equipment.
• Complete required compliance exams in the specified timeframes, such as Anti-Money Laundering, Sanctions, BCM and Basic Financial Crime Concepts.

What you need
• 2–3 years in financial planning or advice in long-term insurance and investment
• NQF 5 FSB approved qualification (120 FAIS credits)
• RE 5 certification
• Fit and proper status for the typical licence categories, and able to maintain it (honesty, integrity, financial solvency)
• Further Education and Training Certificate (FETC): Business, Commerce and Management Studies

What we offer
• Attend training to attain accreditation to market Absa approved products
• Internal FAIS-related programs and courses to attain and maintain the required FAIS credits
• Support from the Regional Manager and practice management specialists on business development

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
